explicitly_excluded: Requiring target applications to use their own native proxy settings
mandatory: Preserve the existing Web panel for adding custom native Windows application paths and assigning proxy nodes
Do not require target applications to support native proxy settings
preferred: Linux-like process-tree isolation, DNS and UDP coverage, and protection against direct fallback
Free long-term operation without usage limits or reminder dialogs
Simple deployment and minimal effect on unselected applications
requirements_revision.latest_user_relaxation: Windows may retain custom application proxy routing as the core requirement, with other isolation properties implemented on a best-effort basis. Lack of strict Linux parity must not veto every functional candidate.

candidates.name: Mihomo TUN plus existing Web panel
candidates.position: Excluded by the user's explicit 2026-10-16 instruction; retained only as historical research
documented_capabilities: Transparent traffic capture through TUN without native proxy configuration in target applications
PROCESS-PATH and PROCESS-NAME routing rules can select a proxy or group; unmatched traffic can use DIRECT
candidates.integration_inference: Translate panel application paths and node selections into Mihomo routing rules and groups. This integration has not been implemented or accepted by this survey.
limitations: auto-route changes host routing; unselected DIRECT traffic can still pass through the core
Executable matching does not itself distinguish separate launch instances or automatically inherit policy across different child executables
A selected UDP flow may continue to later rules when its outbound lacks UDP support; explicit rejection rules and real traffic verification are needed
Not evidence of Linux-equivalent per-instance isolation or persistent selective fail-closed protection

candidates.name: Clew plus Mihomo
candidates.position: Preferred for ready PID/tree APIs and clearer open-source distribution terms; protocol coverage is weaker than ProxiFyre. Not adopted or accepted by project runtime tests.
documented_capabilities: Executable path, command-line and PID controls, dynamic child-tree following, IPv4 TCP and UDP SOCKS5 forwarding, multiple proxy groups
HTTP API for hijack PIDs, automatic rules and proxy groups
MIT application code; bundled WinDivert uses LGPLv3
candidates.integration_inference: Keep the project panel and use Clew API rules and proxy groups against local Mihomo SOCKS endpoints. Administrative lifecycle, local API security and project compatibility still require review and tests.
limitations: Source review on 2026-10-16: TCP and UDP NETWORK workers only request an IPv4 header from WinDivertHelperParsePacket and reinject unchanged when it is absent. IPv6 traffic therefore passes directly in these paths; this is code-derived evidence, not a runtime result.
Uses WinDivert, so it does not independently remove the isolation limitations identified in the earlier ProxyBridge design gate
Release v0.10.0 documents a first-SYN parking watchdog that deliberately releases DIRECT after 20 ms without a decision
Optional DNS forwarding is disabled by default and changes all active IPv4 adapter DNS settings when enabled; restoration after forced termination occurs on a later launch
Runs elevated; existing autostart uses a highest-privilege scheduled task
Upstream release reports exit-IP correctness checks; no project runtime acceptance has been performed

candidates.name: ProxiFyre plus Mihomo
candidates.position: Preferred initial functional validation for the user's relaxed per-application routing core when executable-wide rules suffice and driver licensing fits the deployment; not a stability or runtime acceptance claim
documented_capabilities: Per-executable TCP and UDP forwarding over IPv4 and IPv6 to configurable SOCKS5 endpoints
JSON configuration and Windows service deployment
limitations: Application AGPL licensing does not cover the separately licensed Windows Packet Filter driver
Driver is free for personal and academic use; commercial redistribution requires separate licensing
Executable rules do not establish launch-instance identity or automatic child-tree inheritance
Rule changes require an engine or service restart
Fragmented IPv6 datagrams are passed through directly according to upstream documentation
No demonstrated persistent selective fail-closed protection

comparison_update_2026_10_16.reason_for_ranking_revision: Earlier Clew-first advice emphasized API and child-tree integration. Newly verified IPv6 pass-through weakens its fit for the user's core requirement that selected applications actually use the proxy.
comparison_update_2026_10_16.recommendation: Prefer testing ProxiFyre plus Mihomo for the relaxed custom-application routing core if personal/academic use or suitable driver distribution rights apply. Prefer Clew only when PID/tree controls and distribution terms outweigh its explicitly accepted IPv4 and fail-direct limitations.
comparison_update_2026_10_16.web_panel: Both can retain the existing Web panel. ProxiFyre would need a backend adapter that writes JSON and manages the service; Clew offers HTTP CRUD APIs. Neither project integration has been built by this research.
comparison_update_2026_10_16.stability_evidence: No project side-by-side runtime comparison or benchmark exists; do not claim either is proven more stable or faster.

other_routes_reviewed.Sandboxie: A custom launcher may avoid official Start UI reminders, but stock transparent proxy injection and DNS filtering have certificate gates; free WFP allow/block rules alone do not transparently proxy arbitrary applications.
other_routes_reviewed.AppContainer_LPAC_Job: Available identity and isolation primitives, not a ready transparent proxy backend for arbitrary GUI applications; would reopen compatibility and relay engineering.
other_routes_reviewed.Windows_containers_and_compartments: No identified lightweight supported drop-in equivalent for arbitrary interactive native GUI applications.
other_routes_reviewed.NetFilterSDK_wrappers: Netch, SocksRedirector and related wrappers do not by themselves establish unrestricted free signed-driver licensing.
other_routes_reviewed.DLL_hooks_and_unreleased_drivers: Coverage, compatibility or deployment evidence insufficient to outrank the functional candidates.

recommended_validation_scope: Choose one functional candidate and time-box the initial proof rather than restarting open-ended isolation engineering
Use ordinary applications with native proxy settings disabled, sending unique markers to an independent receiver
Verify actual node A and node B exits, at least two different selected application paths, and an unselected direct-connection control
Check relevant child processes and TCP/UDP/DNS separately; record unsupported behavior explicitly
Do not count an explicit connection to the local SOCKS or HTTP proxy port as proof of transparent interception
Stop and reassess if basic transparent routing cannot be demonstrated within the agreed time box

runtime_followup_2026_10_16.licensing: User confirms personal use; commercial redistribution is not a candidate-selection gate
runtime_followup_2026_10_16.ranking: Clew better matches panel and dynamic-child controls; ProxiFyre remains validated executable-wide alternative. IPv6 and fail-direct limitations remain explicit.
